finding.claim: update_doc (PUT /doc/<doc_id>) never enforces edit authorization: can_edit(g.user, doc) is called but its return value is discarded, so any caller who reaches the route can overwrite the body of any document, including ones they neither own nor are an editor of.
finding.source: Client request to PUT /doc/<doc_id>: doc_id from URL path (docs.py:17) and the 'body' field of the JSON payload (docs.py:20). Caller identity g.user is set by middleware outside this repo.
finding.sink: doc['body'] assignment at docs.py:20 (protected document content write).

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] loaded with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated but result ignored; no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit predicate (docs.py:7-8) is correct but not enforced on this route; require_edit with abort(403) (docs.py:11-13) is not called in update_doc; update_title (docs.py:27) enforces require_edit, showing the intended pattern; no before_request hook or decorator in the repo applies authorization. Authentication middleware that sets g.user is not in the repo and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool and its result is discarded as a bare statement at docs.py:19, so no abort occurs. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) that would abort(403) is not called in update_doc. No before_request hook or decorator exists in the repo (only docs.py is present). The g.user middleware is outside the repo and unverified, but it only supplies identity, not a block on this route.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, discarding its bool result, so the write at docs.py:20 runs for any caller who reaches the route, whereas update_title at docs.py:27 correctly uses require_edit, which aborts with 403 at docs.py:13.
